correctness.rationale: The Hilbert–Schmidt norm is exactly 1/[2α(2α−1)Γ(α)²], making the two products trace class. Spatial reflection unitary swaps the fractional integral and its adjoint and anticommutes with the self-commutator. For integer m, both positive products have identical 2m-th weak derivative, giving polynomial range P_{2m−1}; if a polynomial is killed by their difference, both endpoint derivative jets of orders 0..2m−1 vanish on a common polynomial of degree ≤4m−1, forcing zero. The restriction has rank 2m. For noninteger α, the boundary kernel section has a nonzero x^α times full integer-power series; ordinary analytic terms cannot cancel it, and the coefficient constraints across distinct y-points give invertible Vandermonde matrices of arbitrary size. Kernel continuity turns section independence into infinite operator rank. Reflection gives paired sign inertia. A standalone checker passed 948 finite cross-checks; none is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Self-commutator rank measures a natural nonnormality defect of a canonical fractional-integration semigroup. The theorem gives a complete necessary-and-sufficient characterization over a continuum of orders, an exact nontrivial finite rank and inertia at integer parameters and infinite inertia elsewhere, despite trace-class regularity for all parameters. This integer/noninteger phase boundary is mathematically structural, not an arbitrary slice or a small numerical refinement.
